surfaces.name: Kooky native macOS app (SwiftUI, libghostty terminal)
kooky-cli control CLI and kooky-hook agent hook helper

claims.answer: Native macOS 14+ desktop app and a kooky-cli control CLI; no Windows, Linux, mobile, browser or editor-extension client.

desktop_os.answer: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer, from the DMG release; Package.swift declares only macOS and release v0.51.12 ships a single DMG, so Windows and Linux are unsupported.

mobile_apps.answer: No iOS or Android app in the release or source.

browser.answer: No web client in the source.

cli.answer: kooky-cli opens tabs, resumes conversations, lists, focuses, renames and closes tabs, and reports status.

editor_extensions.answer: No editor extension; the Open in button only hands a directory to other apps.

task_actions.answer: Start an agent tab from the + menu or CLI, type or compose prompts, answer approvals inside the agent terminal and resume conversations by ID; review is limited to a changed-file list with +/- counts.

notifications.answer: macOS notifications and an in-app inbox when an agent waits or a command fails.

cross_device_continuity.answer: State is local to one Mac; no sync or second-device access.

limitations: macOS only; review is limited to file-level changed-line counts; no mobile or browser access.

claims.answer: Fifteen built-in coding CLIs plus any custom command, launched in terminal tabs; Kooky observes them through hooks and process wrappers rather than embedding a harness.

harnesses.answer: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Amp, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Grok Build, Antigravity CLI, Kimi Code, Pi, Oh My Pi, Reasonix, Kiro CLI and Droid.

model_providers.answer: Kooky has no provider layer; models are chosen inside each CLI. Claude-based custom agents can set provider endpoint variables.

custom_adapters.answer: Settings, Agents accepts a name and a command, optionally based on a built-in agent to inherit its launch binary and activity tracking.

session_integration.answer: Launches each agent CLI in a shell tab and watches it through lifecycle hooks, a wrapper script and transcript files; it does not embed the harness or call a session API.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Tabs, panes and workspaces can run different agents at once and the agent panel lists them together.

limitations: Mixed-harness work is side-by-side tabs; activity and tool-pill detail varies by agent and standalone custom commands have no status dot.

claims.answer: Kooky starts the real agent CLI, so existing subscription or API logins in the user shell are used as-is; Kooky has no accounts, credits or billing of its own.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Agents run with whatever native login the CLI already has; Kooky does not intercept it. Codex plan type is displayed.

api_accounts.answer: Claude-based custom agents can carry ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and token variables; other agents use the user shell environment.

vendor_credits.answer: No vendor credits or Kooky account exist.

local_models.answer: No local-model feature; a custom command could launch any CLI.

account_switching.answer: Separate custom Claude entries can hold different endpoint variables; there is no account switcher.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No account of any kind is required to use Kooky.

provider_restrictions.answer: Provider restrictions are in the agents' own terms, not in this repository.

limitations: Credential handling belongs to each agent CLI; only Claude-based custom agents get a product field for environment variables.
claims.unknownReason: Agent providers' subscription terms and restrictions are third-party documents outside the repository.

claims.answer: Install the DMG, bypass Gatekeeper once (adhoc-signed), open any folder as a workspace and pick an agent from the + menu; works with no Git, local Git and cloned remotes, plus SSH hosts.

first_task_setup.answer: README Install: download DMG, drag to Applications, bypass Gatekeeper, open a folder, choose an agent from +.

no_git.answer: Any folder opens as a workspace; git pills appear only inside repositories.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Worktrees, branch switching and diff counts use the local repository only.

hosted_git.answer: Cloned repositories work like local ones; the repo pill opens the remote on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket without any integration login.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: README documents macOS 14+, Gatekeeper bypass paths and build prerequisites (Xcode 26+).

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: File, New SSH Workspace attaches a workspace to an existing host; it does not provision or install anything on it.

limitations: Adhoc-signed, not notarized: first launch needs a manual Gatekeeper bypass; no managed cloud; SSH workspaces need a host the user already runs.

claims.answer: kooky-cli plus kooky:// deep links drive a running app over an owner-only local unix socket; there is no HTTP API, SDK, MCP server or webhook.

cli.answer: kooky-cli open, resume, list --json, focus, close, rename and status.

api.answer: The CLI and hooks speak a versioned JSON protocol over a unix socket; it is internal and undocumented as an API.

mcp_server.answer: Kooky does not expose an MCP server.

operations.answer: Create (open, resume), inspect (list, status), focus, rename and close tabs; no steer, approve, stop-agent or review operations.

authentication.answer: Commands flow only through a local socket with mode 0600; kooky:// links cannot carry commands.

stability.answer: The envelope carries a protocolVersion and the app refuses newer requests; there is no stability guarantee or deprecation policy.

limitations: Local-only; cannot send input, answer approvals, stop an agent or read diffs; socket protocol is not documented as a public API.

claims.answer: Kooky is not an MCP client or plugin host; MCP servers, skills and instruction files belong to each launched agent. Custom agents and Terminal presets are the only extension points.

mcp_client.answer: Kooky is not an MCP client; the launched agents manage their own MCP configuration.

custom_tools.answer: Custom agents and Terminal presets add launch entries, not agent tools.

instructions_import.answer: Kooky imports no instruction files; agents read their own.

permission_scope.answer: No product-level permission scopes for integrations.

integration_owner.answer: Every connection is owned by the launched agent CLI; Kooky only starts it and reads hooks.

limitations: No product-managed MCP, plugin or skill system; integration setup is inherited entirely from the underlying agent CLI.

claims.answer: Native macOS app written in Swift with SwiftUI and AppKit views, rendering terminals with the libghostty GPU engine; no web view, Electron or Tauri.

desktop_implementation.answer: Swift package (swift-tools 6.2, macOS 14) with SwiftUI/AppKit and libghostty; README says SwiftUI-native.

hybrids.answer: No Electron, Tauri or web hybrid found; terminals are native views over libghostty.

implementation_evidence.answer: Package.swift targets and the LibghosttyEngine source at the pinned commit.

limitations: Implementation detail only; says nothing about responsiveness.

claims.answer: Steer by typing in the agent terminal or the prompt composer; closing a tab stops it; waiting agents raise notifications and amber dots. No pause, no escalation.

pause.answer: No pause control beyond the terminal itself.

stop.answer: Closing a tab terminates its foreground process group after a bounded grace period, with an optional confirm-close setting.

resume.answer: Conversations resume by exact session ID after relaunch or from history.

steer.answer: Type into the terminal or the Cmd+L prompt composer.

notifications.answer: macOS notifications plus an inbox for waiting agents and failed commands.

pending_decisions.answer: A waiting dot (including pending tool approval) flags it; the decision itself is made inside the agent.

visible_errors.answer: Tabs and workspaces turn red when the last command exits non-zero, with exit code and duration on hover.

chat_terminal_parity.answer: The terminal is the only surface, so there is nothing to diverge.

retained_history.answer: Agent conversation history is browsable and resumable; scrollback is lost on quit.

limitations: No pause or escalation; stop is closing the tab; pending decisions are answered inside the agent TUI.

claims.answer: The agent panel and sidebar show every agent and workspace across windows ordered by attention; there are no epics, dependencies or workload view.

fleet_fixture.answer: Agent panel lists all agents with state across windows sorted waiting, failed, running, idle.

attention.answer: Waiting agents sort first and carry amber dots and notifications.

history.answer: Session history lists past conversations; no per-fleet timeline.

navigation_errors.answer: Clicking a row jumps to the tab; failed commands show red dots and inbox entries.

fixture_mode.answer: Not applicable; there is no fixture mode.

limitations: No parent/child, dependency or workload views.

claims.answer: Opening an agent is one click from the + menu with no preset; Settings configures agents, Terminal presets and launch options, with no natural-language setup or role UI.

quick_task.answer: Pick an agent from + and start; the agent boots before the first prompt prints.

presets.answer: Terminal presets (pinned directory) and per-agent launch options exist; no workflow presets.

agent_configuration.answer: Custom agents can add launch options and environment; model and effort are set inside the agent.

in_run_changes.answer: The user can type into the running agent; Kooky offers no run-level change.

discoverability.answer: The + menu and Quick Open list every agent and preset.

auth_friction.answer: No Kooky login; existing agent logins apply.

limitations: No growth path from a quick task to a structured effort; no role views.

claims.answer: Agents run locally on the Mac or, for SSH workspaces, inside plain ssh sessions on a host the user controls; Kooky has no managed or hosted execution.

local.answer: Default mode: agents run in local PTYs.

byo_remote.answer: SSH workspaces start tabs and agents on a user-owned host via ssh with shared ControlMaster connections.

hybrid.answer: Local and SSH workspaces can be open side by side.

provisioning.answer: Kooky does not provision remote hosts.

payer.answer: The user pays for their own machines and agent subscriptions; Kooky is free.

expiry.answer: No lifetime limits; sessions end with the ssh connection or app.

client_disconnect.answer: A plain ssh session ends when the connection or the app ends; keep-awake only stops the Mac sleeping.

limitations: SSH tabs are live ssh connections, not detached remote sessions; there is no vendor cloud and no provisioning.

claims.answer: Git worktrees on request (Create Worktree creates a branch folder nested under its repo); otherwise agents share the opened folder. No container, VM or OS sandbox.

checkout.answer: Default workspace is the opened folder, shared by all its tabs.

branch.answer: Worktree creation targets a new or existing branch.

worktree.answer: Create Worktree, adopt mode and optional removal with branch delete.

os_sandbox.answer: No OS sandbox; only macOS secure keyboard input and clipboard confirmation.

filesystem.answer: No filesystem boundary beyond worktree folders.

process.answer: No process boundary; agents are child processes of the user shell.

secrets.answer: Custom agent environment variables stay out of the shell export for Claude entries, via a settings file; no secret isolation.

code_separation.answer: Worktrees keep branches separate on disk.

security_boundary.answer: None; a worktree is not a security boundary.

limitations: A worktree separates files only; agents run as the user with full access.

claims.answer: Layout, cwd, worktree and SSH-host metadata restore on relaunch and agent conversations resume by exact session ID; scrollback and running processes cannot survive quit.

client_disconnect.answer: There is no separate client; SSH tabs end when the connection drops and reconnect on next spawn.

worker_crash.answer: No worker process model; a crash writes a local stderr log only.

transcript_reload.answer: Agent history can be re-read and resumed; Kooky scrollback is not persisted.

process_reconnect.answer: Processes cannot be reattached after quit; panes respawn.

task_resume.answer: Agents resume their exact conversation after relaunch or from history.

state_reconstruction.answer: state.json rebuilds windows, panes, workspaces, worktrees and SSH hosts.

context_loss.answer: Terminal scrollback and unsaved shell input are lost; agent context returns through resume.

duplicate_actions.answer: No documented guard against agent repeating actions after resume.

manual_repair.answer: Users reopen missing worktrees or SSH hosts; entries whose directory is gone are cleaned at launch.

multi_day_continuity.answer: Conversations resume from agent transcripts on the same Mac, with no compute replacement concept.

limitations: Processes and scrollback are lost on quit or disconnect; resume depends on each agent CLI.

claims.answer: Kooky does not install dependencies or manage services; the status bar shows Node, Python venv, proxy and branch state and can switch Node versions and branches.

dependencies.answer: Status bar detects Node and venv and can run a Node version switch in the shell.

ports.answer: Session Info lists a tab's listening ports and opens them in a browser; nothing allocates ports.

remote_setup.answer: SSH agents start with the remote shell setup loaded so nvm-installed tools resolve.

evidence.title: Kooky README
evidence.locator: Features; CLI; Install; Build from source
evidence.finding: Native macOS 14+ terminal with sidebar workspaces, splits, fifteen one-click agents with activity dots, worktrees, SSH workspaces, keep-awake, notifications, history, kooky-cli; MIT; no accounts or telemetry; adhoc-signed DMG.

evidence.title: Kooky changelog
evidence.finding: Frequent small releases; v0.51.0 introduced kooky-cli; v0.51.12 added keyboard shortcuts and hidden history rows; no dated roadmap.

evidence.title: MIT License
evidence.finding: MIT License, copyright 2026 kooky contributors.

evidence.title: Third-party notices
evidence.finding: Bundled fonts (OFL) and Shiki theme palettes (MIT) retain upstream licenses; libghostty is linked as a dependency.

evidence.title: Kooky v0.51.12 release
evidence.finding: Single asset Kooky-v0.51.12.dmg (10.1 MB), published 2026-10-12; no Windows, Linux, iOS or Android artifact.

evidence.title: GitHub repository metadata
evidence.finding: 656 stars, MIT, last push 2026-10-12, created 2026-05-08, no homepage set, not archived.

evidence.title: Swift package manifest
evidence.finding: macOS 14 floor; targets Kooky (app), KookyKit, KookyHook, kooky-cli and KookyHookKit; links GhosttyKit; no other platform.

evidence.title: Built-in agent templates
evidence.finding: Templates for terminal, claude-code, codex, gemini, opencode, amp, cursor, copilot, grok, antigravity, kimi, pi, omp, reasonix, kiro and droid; each launches the vendor CLI under a shell wrapper and resumes by exact conversation ID.

evidence.title: Custom agents and environment
evidence.finding: User-defined agents (name + command, optional built-in base) with per-agent .env-style environment variables for Claude-based entries; KOOKY_-prefixed keys are dropped.

evidence.title: Hook wiring for agents
evidence.finding: Kooky passes a generated hooks file to claude with --settings and writes managed hook blocks for other agents so lifecycle events reach the app.

evidence.title: Local unix socket server
evidence.finding: App owns a unix socket (mode 0600) that the hook helper and kooky-cli connect to; no network listener.

evidence.title: CLI wire protocol
evidence.finding: Verbs: open, resume, list, focus, close, status, rename; versioned envelope.

evidence.title: CLI request handling
evidence.finding: Dispatches list, close, open, resume, focus, rename; refuses a protocol version newer than the app.

evidence.title: kooky-cli entry point
evidence.finding: kooky-cli parses verbs and prints one reason line on failure; exit code 0 means accepted.

evidence.title: kooky:// deep links
evidence.finding: kooky://resume?agent=&id=[&cwd=] with strict character validation; links cannot carry prompts or commands.

evidence.title: Agent session history
evidence.finding: Scans each agent own transcript directory (for example ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions) to list and resume past conversations; read-only.

evidence.title: Codex usage gauge
evidence.finding: Reads Codex rollout token_count events for 5-hour and weekly rate-limit percentages, plan type and context-window occupancy; display only.

evidence.title: Git worktree manager
evidence.finding: Creates worktrees on a new or existing branch, adopts existing ones, removes with optional branch delete.

evidence.title: SSH workspace wrapper
evidence.finding: SSH workspaces use ssh with ControlMaster multiplexing; every tab runs a plain ssh session and agents are started on the remote through the wrapper.

evidence.title: New SSH workspace sheet
evidence.finding: File menu sheet that records a remote host for a workspace.

evidence.title: Keep-awake including closed lid
evidence.finding: Fixed two-verb root helper around pmset -a disablesleep with a one-time admin authorization; keeps the Mac awake while agents work.

evidence.title: Notification manager
evidence.finding: macOS notifications when a background agent waits or a command fails; settings toggle each kind.

evidence.title: State persistence
evidence.finding: state.json keeps workspaces, panes, cwd, worktree and SSH host; scrollback and processes cannot survive PTY exit, so panes respawn.

evidence.title: Update checker
evidence.finding: Manual Help menu check calls api.github.com releases/latest; no startup poll; only network call found in the app.

evidence.title: Git status and diff pill
evidence.finding: Status bar shows branch and git diff --numstat counts; popover lists changed files with insertions and deletions, not diff hunks.

evidence.title: Agent panel
evidence.finding: Right panel lists every agent across windows sorted attention (waiting), failed, running, idle.

evidence.title: Clipboard confirmation
evidence.finding: Confirmation sheet before risky paste and OSC 52 clipboard access.

evidence.title: Secure keyboard input
evidence.finding: Holds macOS secure keyboard input during password entry.

evidence.title: Local crash forensics
evidence.finding: Writes stderr and exit notes to ~/Library/Logs/kooky/stderr.log; nothing is uploaded.

evidence.title: libghostty terminal engine
evidence.finding: Terminal sessions render through the libghostty xcframework inside SwiftUI/AppKit views.

evidence.title: Session Info panel
evidence.finding: Inspector shows git branch/diff, venv, Node version, process tree with CPU and memory, listening ports and last command exit code.

evidence.title: Kooky pull requests and discussions
evidence.finding: Open pull requests propose Mosh transport, project grouping and SSH ports; no roadmap or announcement.

evidence.title: Bounded search: other clients
evidence.locator: grep -w over Sources and Package.swift for linux, windows, docker, electron, tauri, webview, WKWebView, iOS, android
evidence.finding: No non-macOS client, web client, phone client or editor extension; matches are Swift window objects.

evidence.title: Bounded search: APIs, MCP, webhooks, SDK
evidence.locator: grep -w for mcp, webhook, openapi, NWListener, GraphQL, sdk over Sources
evidence.finding: No MCP server or client, webhook, HTTP API or SDK; only the local unix socket CLI.

evidence.title: Bounded search: schedules and triggers
evidence.locator: grep -w for cron, launchd, LaunchAgent, crontab over Sources
evidence.finding: No scheduler or event trigger.

evidence.title: Bounded search: collaboration and enterprise
evidence.locator: grep -w for sso, saml, rbac, invite, multiplayer, presence over Sources
evidence.finding: No accounts, roles, SSO, sharing or multi-user features.

evidence.title: Bounded search: container or VM isolation
evidence.locator: grep -w for docker, podman, lima, colima, qemu, virtualization, sandbox-exec, seatbelt over Sources
evidence.finding: No container, VM or OS sandbox isolation.

evidence.title: Bounded search: cost tracking
evidence.locator: grep -w for usd, dollar, spend, budget, totalCost, pricing over Sources
evidence.finding: No dollar cost, spend, budget or pricing code; only Codex rate-limit percentages.

evidence.title: Bounded search: native issues and tasks
evidence.locator: grep -w for ticket, backlog, kanban, epic, jira, linear over Sources
evidence.finding: No issue, task or ticket entity; workspaces are folders.

evidence.title: Bounded search: delegation and orchestration
evidence.locator: grep -w for subagent, orchestrator, orchestration over Sources
evidence.finding: No coordinator or delegation tool; kooky-cli is a tab-control interface.

evidence.title: Bounded search: pull requests and delivery
evidence.locator: grep for gh pr, pull request, createPR, merge request, git commit, git push over Sources
evidence.finding: No PR, commit, merge or deploy action; git is used read-only plus worktree and branch switching.

evidence.title: Bounded search: telemetry
evidence.locator: grep -i for telemetry, analytics, sentry, posthog, mixpanel, crashreport over Sources, README
evidence.finding: No analytics or crash-reporting client; README says no telemetry; only the manual GitHub update check.

locations.result: v0.51.12 (2026-10-12) is the latest release; release notes list shipped changes only.
Per-release changelog from v0.51.0 to v0.51.12 and earlier; no dated future commitments.
No roadmap section. Says public-distribution signing and notarization will come when there are real users, without a date.
Open pull requests such as project grouping (#85), SSH explicit port (#87) and a Mosh transport (#48) are unmerged proposals, not announcements, and are not treated as shipped.
Linked from the issue-template config as the place for ideas; no dated product announcements read.

Nine open issues as of 2026-11-17; the newest (#89, 2026-11-06) is a split-closing bug. Closed issues are bug reports and small feature requests that shipped (#56 deep links, #57 CLI title and background open); no roadmap or dated announcement.
